title: Analysis of Gene Expression Using RT-qPCR in Blood Stage Plasmodium falciparum
author: Emma Kals
materials: Reagents - Invitogen Thermo Fisher scientific Phasemaker tubes Ref A33248. Zymo research RNA Clean and concentrator - 5 (Cat No R1015).
Using the superscript IV VILO MM with ezDNase enzyme (ThermoFisher 11756050) following the manufacturer’s instructions alongside a no reverse transcription (RT) control.

Cycling conditions; 95 o C for 10 min, followed by 40 cycles of 95 o C for 15 s, 55 o C for 20 s, 60 o Cfor 60 s. Then run a melt curve of 65 o C for 5 s up to 95 o C.– These are standard conditions but will change depending on the size of your amplicon and Tm of your primers. We used a Bio-rad 384 well RT PCR machine (CFX384). The melt curve is to determine if there is any non-specific amplification.

steps.title: Prepare cultures and percoll tubes
steps.instruction: Set up each parasite line in a 150 ml culture at 1 % hematocrit (HCT). For each sample make two 15 ml tubes containing 5 ml Percoll; place tubes in a 37 °C water bath. Warm 35 ml RPMI‑1640 medium plus 3 ml 50 % HCT in a vented flask to 37 °C.

steps.title: Check parasite stage by smear
steps.instruction: At 09:00 am make thin blood smears, stain and verify that the culture is mainly late‑stage schizonts with a few rings, indicating the start of egress.

steps.title: Aspirate media leaving 5 ml
steps.instruction: Using an aspirator, remove all media from each flask leaving exactly 5 ml residual liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend blood and layer over percoll
steps.instruction: Resuspend the packed red blood cells (RBCs) in warm medium, then using a 5 ml pipette set to slow, carefully layer the suspension over the 5 ml Percoll in the 15 ml tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate stages
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 2600 rpm for 11 min with brake = 1 and acceleration = 3.

steps.title: Collect late stages and incubate
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, remove the late‑stage band and return it to the original flask that already contains 35 ml medium and 3 ml blood (50 % HCT). Place the flask in a gassed incubator at 37 °C for 3.5 h. Meanwhile keep RPMI, additional medium and 5 % sorbitol in a 37 °C water bath.

steps.title: Post‑incubation media removal and percoll layering
steps.instruction: After 3.5 h, aspirate all but 5 ml of the flask medium if the sample has sedimented; if not, pellet the cells by a standard parasite spin (see step 9). Resuspend the RBCs in medium and layer over 5 ml Percoll in a fresh 5 ml tube.

steps.title: Second Percoll centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the new tube at 2600 rpm for 11 min (brake = 1, acceleration = 3).

steps.title: Resuspend rings in sorbitol and warm
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant (including any remaining late‑stage infected RBCs). Resuspend the pellet, which now contains newly invaded rings, in 5 ml 5 % sorbitol and transfer to a 50 ml tube. Place the tube in a 37 °C water bath for 5 min.

steps.title: Pellet and resuspend in warm RPMI
steps.instruction: Pellet the sorbitol‑treated cells by a standard parasite spin, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 20 ml warm RPMI‑1640.

steps.title: Pellet and incubate overnight
steps.instruction: Pellet again by standard parasite spin, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in the original flask medium (35 ml medium + 3 ml blood, 50 % HCT). Keep the flask at room temperature until 19:00 h, then place it back in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Repeat synchronization on Thursday
steps.instruction: On Thursday repeat steps 2–10 (starting with the aspirate step). At the end of the day leave the flask at room temperature overnight until 19:00 h on Friday, then return to 37 °C. If parasitemia is high (≈2 weeks of synchronisation), let ~1/3 of the culture reinvade and treat the remaining 2/3 with Compound 2.

steps.title: Isolate late stages and add Compound 2
steps.instruction: Isolate late stages using 5 ml Percoll in a 15 ml tube as before. Collect the late‑stage band, transfer to a new 15 ml tube and add 5 ml warm RPMI. Resuspend the pellet in 40 ml medium in a vented 250 ml flask and add PKG inhibitor Compound 2 (4‑[7‑[(dimethylamino)methyl]‑2‑(4‑fluorophenyl)imidazo[1,2‑α]pyridine‑3‑yl]pyrimidin‑2‑amine) to a final concentration of 1 µM. Incubate at 37 °C in a gassed incubator for 3.5 h.

steps.title: Prepare saponin/PBS solutions and chill
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 × PBS/0.1 % saponin by diluting 1 ml of 1 % saponin stock into 9 ml PBS. Keep the 0.1 % saponin solution and PBS on ice together with a 50 ml Falcon tube and 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Pellet parasites, wash, and split
steps.instruction: Spin the culture to pellet parasites; the supernatant should no longer be red (repeat the wash if it is). Remove supernatant, flick the pellet to remove residual liquid, resuspend in 200 µl PBS and split the suspension into two 1.5 ml tubes.

steps.title: Add TriZol and incubate
steps.instruction: To each tube add 1000 µl TriZol in the fume hood, mix well and incubate at 37 °C for 5 min. Afterwards place the tubes on ice (or store at –80 °C if RNA extraction will be delayed).

steps.title: Pellet, wash with PBS/saponin, ice incubation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge to pellet, carefully discard supernatant without disturbing the pellet, then resuspend the pellet in 1 ml 1 × PBS/0.1 % saponin. Keep on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Pellet cultures at 1100 rpm and wash
steps.instruction: Pellet the cultures in a 50 ml Falcon tube at 1100 rpm for 5 min. Wash the pellet with 5 ml ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge and discard supernatant. Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml ice‑cold 0.1 % saponin, transfer to a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube and keep on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Thaw Trizol samples and add extra Trizol if needed
steps.instruction: For each sample thaw one tube containing 100 µl of the PBS‑saponin suspension and 900 µl Trizol. If clumps are visible, add additional Trizol and heat at 37 °C for 5 min to dissolve all material.

steps.title: Phase separation with phasemaker tubes
steps.instruction: Spin a Phasemaker tube (one per sample) at 12 000 g for 30 s. Transfer 1 ml of the Trizol‑containing sample into the Phasemaker tube and incubate at room temperature for 5 min. Add 200 µl chloroform, shake vigorously for 15 s, incubate 3 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 12 000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the top aqueous phase and transfer it to a new tube.

steps.title: Bind RNA to Zymo column with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ethanol to the aqueous phase (e.g., 450 µl), mix, and load the mixture onto a Zymo Clean & Concentrator‑5 spin column. Spin at room temperature at 14 000 g for 30 s and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash column with wash buffer
steps.instruction: Add 400 µl Zymo wash buffer to the column, spin at 14 000 g for 30 s, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: On‑column DNase I digestion
steps.instruction: Prepare DNase I mix by combining 5 µl DNase I with 35 µl DNA Digestion Buffer. Add the 40 µl mix to the column, incubate at room temperature for 15 min.

steps.title: Wash column with RNA prep and wash buffers
steps.instruction: Add 400 µl RNA prep buffer, spin at 14 000 g for 30 s and discard flow‑through. Then add 700 µl RNA wash buffer, spin and discard. Add a second 400 µl RNA wash buffer, spin and discard.

steps.title: Elute RNA in RNase‑free water
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a clean tube and spin for 60 s to remove residual wash buffer. Add 20 µl RNase‑free water directly onto the column matrix, let stand 5 min, then spin to elute RNA.

steps.title: Quantify RNA and assess purity
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration with a NanoDrop; acceptable A260/A280 ratio is ~2.0 (≥1.8). If the ratio is <1.7, perform additional clean‑up (e.g., ethanol precipitation) noting that this may cause RNA loss.

steps.title: DNase treatment of RNA with ezDNase
steps.instruction: For each sample use 1 µg RNA. In a PCR strip combine 2 µg RNA (1 µg for the RT reaction and 1 µg for the No‑RT control) with 2 µl ezDNase enzyme, 2 µl 10× Buffer, and water to a final volume of 20 µl. Incubate at 37 °C for 2 min.

steps.title: Set up RT and No‑RT reactions
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µl of each DNase‑treated sample to a new tube. Add 4 µl Master Mix (MM) and 6 µl nuclease‑free water to each tube. To the RT tube add the RT Master Mix; to the No‑RT tube add the No‑RT Master Mix (leaving an empty tube between them).

steps.title: Thermocycler program for cDNA synthesis
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a thermocycler and run: 25 °C for 10 min, 50 °C for 10 min, then 85 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Store cDNA
steps.instruction: Store the resulting cDNA at –20 °C for long‑term storage; it remains stable for days‑weeks at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR master mix
steps.instruction: Use SYBR Power SYBR Green PCR Master Mix (Fisher Scientific 4367659). Prepare primers at 500‑800 nM (e.g., 650 nM). For a 10 µl reaction combine: 5 µl Master Mix, 0.65 µl primer mix, 1 µl cDNA (10 ng), and nuclease‑free water to 10 µl. Prepare a master mix for each primer set and keep on ice.

steps.title: Dispense master mix and cDNA into plate
steps.instruction: Aliquot 9 µl of the appropriate master mix into each well of a 384‑well qPCR plate. Add 1 µl of cDNA (10 ng) to each sample well; add 1 µl nuclease‑free water to no‑template control wells. Seal the plate with a plastic cover and spin down briefly.
